# A refund written by hand, naming no owner lot.
#
# The debit on the receivable belongs to no lot, and that is how raising a
# receivable by hand looks too (fx_settlement_arriving_as_cad.txt raises one
# exactly this way). The two are the same three lines, so the debit is read as
# the receivable it resembles and establishes a basis: 100.00 USD the customer
# owes. Nothing in the file says otherwise.
#
# `lot_owner:` is what says otherwise. With it the debit settles the owner lot
# no invoice owns — a refund — and establishes nothing
# (fx_refund_usd_prepayment.txt). It is the same rule the credit side already
# runs on, and it runs in both directions or neither.
#
# What this fixture produces: `fx-balances` lists 100.00 USD at 1.37 CAD/USD
# on the receivable, for money that has left the bank. Read as a receivable
# that is what it should say; read as a refund it is wrong, and the file has
# to say which it is.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.
2026-01-01 open Assets
	type: Asset
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Bank:USD
	type: Bank
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-01-01 open Assets:Accounts Receivable USD
	type: Accounts Receivable
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"

2026-02-01 * "Refund the customer, naming no lot"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Accounts Receivable USD 100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.37"
		value: "137.00"
	Assets:Bank:USD -100.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "1.37"
		value: "-137.00"
